title: Palak Paneer
subtitle: Creamy Indian spinach curry with paneer
excerpt: Palak paneer is a smooth, creamy spinach curry with firm cubes of fresh cheese. The spinach is blanched and blended to give the sauce its vibrant colour and silky texture. Paneer holds its shape during cooking and absorbs the spiced sauce around it.
sourceNotes: Palak paneer is found across North India and is one of the most popular vegetarian dishes in Indian restaurants worldwide. Paneer -- fresh unsalted curd cheese -- is made by curdling heated milk with lemon juice or vinegar. It has been made across the subcontinent for centuries.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The spinach sauce can be made and blended 1 day ahead. Fry the paneer and add just before serving.

content.text: Frying the paneer cubes before adding them to the sauce gives them a golden crust and stops them becoming too soft. Do not skip this step. If you cannot find paneer, firm tofu works as a substitute.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry the paneer cubes in batches for 2 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining oil. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cumin and coriander. Stir for 1 minute. Add the drained spinach and 100ml of water. Stir well and cook for 3 minutes.
Use a hand blender to blend the spinach mixture until smooth. Return to the heat.
Add salt and garam masala. Stir in the cream. Simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Add the fried paneer cubes. Stir gently and cook for 2 minutes until the paneer is heated through. Serve with rice or roti.

items.cause: The spinach was cooked too long after blending
items.fix: Blend and add cream quickly; do not boil the sauce hard after blending

items.symptom: Paneer is crumbling in the pan
items.cause: Frying a very fresh or soft block that has not been pressed
items.fix: Press the paneer block between paper towels with a weight for 15 minutes before cutting and frying

items.cause: Spinach was very dry after thawing
items.fix: Stir in 2 to 3 tablespoons of water after blending and adjust consistency

content.text: Palak paneer is one of the most recognisable Indian dishes outside India. It is served in virtually every Indian restaurant in the UK and North America. At home in India, it is straightforward everyday food -- greens and fresh cheese, spiced and enriched with a little cream. The smooth, restaurant-style blended version shown here is the most common form.
